newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Pakistan explains Taleban support to Central Asia.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan explains Taleban support to Central Asia.

text.p: Pakistan Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan began a visit to the ex-Soviet states of Central Asia on Wednesday intent on explaining his country's support for Afghanistan's purist Islamic Taleban militia.
"The purpose of my visit here is to explain our position on the recognition of the Taleban government," Khan told reporters on his arrival in the Kazakh capital Almaty.
The Pakistani embassy in Almaty said Khan would also visit Afghanistan's neighbour, Tajikistan.

Central Asian leaders, many of them former Communist Party bosses, are deeply suspicious of the Taleban's fundamentalist brand of Islam and fear Afghan chaos could spill across their borders threatening their own stability.
Uzbekistan's president, Islam Karimov, has been especially vocal in his opposition to the Taleban.

Pakistan is quietly promoting the Taleban in Central Asia as the only means of bringing peace to the country, which would in turn open up new routes to export oil, gas and other goods from Central Asia direct to booming south Asian markets.
The resource-rich but land-locked region is also desperate to break decades of dependence on former colonial master Russia for export routes.
Khan said an Afghan peace could mean: "The Central Asian republics will have access through communications, roads, railways, pipelines into the Arabian Sea through Pakistan and Afghanistan."
Pakistan recognised the Taleban, which now controls most of Afghanistan, late last month, followed by Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.
Khan said he would discuss Pakistan's proposal of an intra-Afghan dialogue under United Nations auspices with Kazakh Foreign Minister Kasymzhomart Tokayev.
Afghan neighbours Iran, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan have already been invited to the meeting, for which no date has been set.
U.N. officials have said they see little chance of any serious talks between the belligerents.
Khan travels on to Tajikistan on Thursday.
